searchText: b"h phase 1 — boundless brainstorm: the portal that can hold anything the awtsmoos creates each possible form before any schema can name its edge; awtsmoos.com should let data become useful without forcing tomorrow's invention through yesterday's wedge. universal resource possibilities 1. a resource envelope with identity, canonical type, human title, raw data, schema reference, version, timestamps, links, capabilities, permissions, provenance, presentation hints, and relationships. 2. arbitrary namespaced types such as awtsmoos.document, social.post, game.save, media.video, or types invented later without core client changes. 3. type definitions that are themselves resources and can be queried, versioned, documented, diffed, deprecated, extended, and inspected. 4. schema adapters capable of understanding existing json schema like shapes without demanding immediate migration. 5. scalar fields, nested objects, arrays, tuples, unions, enums, maps, trees, graphs, matrices, spatial geometry, temporal intervals, binary/media references, opaque extension values, and calculated fields. 6. field metadata for label, description, units, format, semantic role, examples, readonly state, sensitivity, indexing, display priority, and grouping. 7. stable semantic roles such as title, subtitle, body, thumbnail, status, owner, timestamps, geographic point, duration, color, code, or monetary value without coupling to exact field names. 8. safe presentation hints: preferred renderer, density, grouping, primary actions, column suggestions, media aspect, reading width, and layout primitives—but never arbitrary executable css or html from the server. 9. a universal capability vocabulary: read, create, update, delete, duplicate, archive, publish, unpublish, share, export, download, upload, move, reorder, execute, cancel, retry, transform, relate, comment, approve, inspect. 10. custom namespaced capabilities that still describe their input/output schema. 11. action descriptors with method, endpoint/operation identifier, input schema, confirmation requirement, idempotency, destructive level, progress mode, output resource type, reversibility, and permission state. 12. action invocations returning typed resources or typed jobs, never mysterious booleans when a richer result exists. 13. structured errors with code, title, explanation, field issues, request correlation, retryability, causes, safe diagnostics, and suggested user actions. 14. validation issues with machine path, human message, rule, severity, correction hint, and optional alternative values. 15. collection resources with items, cursor/page metadata, total/estimated count, facets, available sorting, available filters, grouping, summaries, bulk capabilities, and saved view links. 16. structured queries made of predicates rather than url string invention: equality, range, text, membership, existence, logical groups, relationship traversal, temporal/spatial conditions, projection, sort, aggregation, grouping, pagination. 17. query descriptions that the ui can convert into search bars, filter sheets, facets, chips, grouped results, exports, and api examples. 18. saved views as resources containing query + projection + layout preference + owner + sharing + permissions. 19. universal search returning heterogeneous typed resources with highlights, ranking explanation, type facets, and continuation cursors. 20. relationship descriptors supporting parent/child, belongs to, contains, references, created by, derived from, related to, mentions, uses, depends on, custom relations, and reverse/backlink discovery. 21. relationship traversal that can power breadcrumbs, dependency trees, backlinks, related items, graph visualization, and provenance trails. 22. revision/history resources with immutable revision ids, actor, timestamp, cause, diff summary, parent revision, restored from, and rollback capability where safe. 23. provenance chains that distinguish user authored, imported, generated, transformed, synchronized, cloned, or derived data. 24. transformation receipts storing source resources, transformer id/version, configuration, environment metadata, result hashes, output resources, warnings, and reproducibility state. 25. first class long running jobs with queued/running/waiting/succeeded/failed/cancelled states, progress, stages, logs, outputs, cancellation, retry policy, and parent/child jobs. 26. streaming resource updates through sse/websocket/events while retaining snapshot get semantics for reliability. 27. event resources describing changes, actions, resource lifecycle, job progress, collaboration, or domain events with cursor based replay. 28. transform definitions that describe accepted resource types, configuration schema, output types, cost/capability hints, side effects, and deterministic/nondeterministic behavior. 29. pipelines/workflows as resources composed of transformations, branches, guards, retries, approvals, and outputs. 30. templates as typed generators: declared input schema, output resource type, renderer hints, version, author, provenance, and examples. 31. form definitions as resources able to produce polished mobile/desktop forms using universal field renderers. 32. safe layout definitions made from constrained primitives such as stack, cluster, grid, split, section, tabs, disclosure, toolbar, sidebar, media, table, timeline, and inspector. 33. representation negotiation: canonical json, compact json, csv, text, binary, image/video/audio, downloadable archive, rendered preview, or stream where the type supports it. 34. binary resources that keep metadata and bytes separate, with hashes, sizes, media types, renditions, thumbnails, transcoding/scan state, and download capabilities. 35. localization data for labels/descriptions and logical direction behavior without duplicating the entire resource. 36. field level permission hints while keeping enforcement server side. 37. action level permission hints so impossible controls never appear enabled. 38. sensitive fields that can be omitted, redacted, masked, or capability gated without changing the enclosing resource identity. 39. resource ownership and tenancy metadata where current authorization architecture supports it. 40. etags/revision tokens and optimistic concurrency for safe editing. 41. idempotency keys for mutating actions that can safely support retries. 42. partial success results for bulk actions with per item outcomes and retry selections. 43. import/export definitions that expose accepted formats, validation, preview/dry run, mapping, progress, and resulting resources. 44. data quality metadata: stale, incomplete, inferred, approximate, generated, verified, conflict, missing dependency, or validation warning. 45. computed values that expose dependencies and readonly semantics instead of pretending to be stored source fields. 46. extensible schema vocabulary via namespaced annotations rather than central schema rewrites. 47. compatibility aliases for old field names/types/actions during migrations. 48. type lineage/extension so specialized resource types inherit semantic contracts without unsafe class like server coupling. 49. capability discovery from a root portal document instead of hardcoding hundreds of urls. 50. generated openapi/json schema/doc material from the same authoritative definitions when compatible with existing tooling. universal ui possibilities 51. a default renderer for any resource that never emits raw unstyled json unless the user explicitly chooses developer/raw mode. 52. renderer registry keyed by semantic capability and type, with fallback chain: specialized → semantic role → generic schema → raw inspector. 53. field renderer registry for text, number, boolean, enum, date/time, duration, currency, rich text, code, json, media, file, relationship, list, object, tree, graph, map, coordinates, color, status, and unknown values. 54. universal card, detail, summary, row, search result, picker, compact, editor, history, relationship, and developer inspector views. 55. a stable ui foundation that styles every native html element intentionally before page specific css loads. 56. shared tokens for typography, spacing, radii, borders, elevation, focus, status colors, width constraints, motion, safe areas, and readable contrast. 57. no neon/glass/futuristic default: solid surfaces, subtle borders, restrained shadows, calm typography, sparse accent use. 58. mobile composition rules: drawers/sheets instead of squeezed sidebars, stacked forms, full width important actions, compact sticky headers, reachable controls, safe area insets, dynamic viewport units, and keyboard aware layouts. 59. universal interactive states: hover, active, focus visible, disabled, busy, selected, destructive, success, error, stale, offline. 60. universal list treatment distinguishing prose lists, navigation, rows, feeds, selectable collections, trees, and grouped results. 61. universal table shell with sticky header option, horizontal overflow container, responsive column priority, row actions, empty/loading/error state, and mobile card fallback where semantics permit. 62. universal dialogs that become sheets/full screen on narrow viewports and always manage focus, escape, backdrop, scroll locking, and return focus. 63. universal menus/popovers with collision handling, max height, scrolling, keyboard traversal, typeahead where appropriate, and mobile adaptation. 64. universal loading states that preserve layout and avoid jumpiness. 65. universal empty states with explanation and contextual next action. 66. universal errors near the affected resource/action with structured detail disclosure and request correlation. 67. universal toast system limited to transient confirmation; persistent problems remain in context. 68. universal search/filter experience with mobile filter sheet, selected filter chips, counts, saved views, and shareable url state. 69. universal relationship panel showing breadcrumbs, parents, children, backlinks, dependencies, and related items when available. 70. universal history panel with revision timeline, actor/cause, diff, restore eligibility, and provenance. 71. universal action bar derived from capability descriptors while still allowing bespoke ordering/placement per specialized renderer. 72. universal resource inspector for permitted users: type, id, schema, capabilities, permissions, relationships, api links, revisions, provenance, raw representation, renderer chosen, diagnostics. 73. unknown resource presentation that clearly labels unknown/custom type while still showing intelligible fields and actions. 74. unknown field presentation that never crashes: readable label, safe serialized value, expandable structure, copy affordance. 75. rtl/logical css by default so hebrew and mixed direction interfaces do not require bespoke rewrites. 76. reduced motion support at the token/primitive level. 77. minimum target sizes and accessible name enforcement through runtime audit. 78. universal :focus visible contract and no focus removal without replacement. 79. safe zoom and readable text sizing; no user scalable lockouts. 80. width discipline: prose constrained, forms constrained, media intentional, dashboards elastic, cinema wide whitespace useful rather than stretched. 81. progressive enhancement: readable semantic markup exists before optional javascript upgrades. 82. offline/stale ui indicating what remains available and what requires reconnection. 83. optimistic ui limited to reversible/safe actions with conflict recovery. 84. skeletons only where they meaningfully preserve structure; simple spinners not sprayed everywhere. 85. touch drag/reorder alternatives that also work with keyboard and explicit move controls. 86. responsive navigation patterns selected by information architecture rather than one global hamburger everywhere. 87. stable scroll restoration and url state for tabs/search/filter views. 88. long names/urls/hebrew/localized text handled intentionally by wrap/clamp/ellipsis rules. 89. media surfaces with aspect control, loading/error placeholders, fullscreen, captions/subtitles, and mobile orientation behavior. 90. code/json surfaces with scroll/wrap toggle, copy, readable line height, and no page level overflow. 91. forms grouped by semantic sections with labels, descriptions, validation, dirty/saving/saved status, and destructive actions isolated. 92. settings pages with desktop section navigation and mobile jump control. 93. game/editor/media routes allowed strong bespoke identity while inheriting stable controls, errors, dialogs, accessibility, and mobile safety. 94. audit enforcement so an unstyled visible native control becomes a measurable regression finding. 95. screenshot matrices across 360x800, 390x844, 768x1024, 1440x900, 1920x1080 for representative page families. 96. visual density modes only where real domains need them, not as random user settings. 97. dark mode as semantic token variation if existing product behavior supports it; no theme specific component forks. 98. internationalized dates/numbers/currencies from semantic formats, not manually concatenated strings. 99. copy/share/download affordances derived from resource capabilities. 100. everything exciting lives under the floorboards; the human sees calm, obvious, dependable software. phase 1 boundary this is possibility, not permission. no item becomes implementation until current router, schema, ui, tests, and consumers prove where the compatibility boundary belongs.
